text.en: Why does a giraffe have such a long neck? Two great thinkers gave two different answers, and one of them is supported by modern science.

Evolution is the gradual change in living organisms over time that produces new species through natural selection.
Lamarck (1809, Philosophie Zoologique) proposed inheritance of acquired characters or use and disuse: organs that are used grow stronger and those unused degenerate.
His principles: internal vital force, environment and new needs, use and disuse, and inheritance of acquired characters; he explained the giraffe's long neck by constant stretching.
Charles Darwin voyaged on H.M.S. Beagle (1831-1835), visited the Galapagos, and published On the Origin of Species in 1859.
Darwin's principles: overproduction, struggle for existence, variations, survival of the fittest (natural selection) and origin of species.
Struggle for existence may be intraspecific, interspecific or environmental.
Variation is the difference among individuals of a species and the raw material of evolution; somatic variations are not inherited, germinal variations are.
Continuous variations are small and fluctuating, like height and skin colour; discontinuous variations arise suddenly by mutation, for example Ancon sheep, as in De Vries' mutation theory.
Mutation (errors in DNA, UV rays, chemicals) causes variation in a single individual.

problem.en: Explain the giraffe's long neck according to Lamarck and according to Darwin.

text.en: Lamarck: giraffes stretched their necks to reach leaves, and the lengthened neck was passed on to offspring.
Darwin: giraffes varied in neck length, and those with longer necks got more food and survived.

why.en: Natural selection of a favourable variation.

text.en: Modern genetics supports Darwin because acquired traits are not inherited.

why.en: Only germinal variations are passed on.

prompt.en: List the five principles of Darwinism in order.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking Darwin supported use and disuse

points.en: Lamarck: use and disuse and inheritance of acquired characters.
Darwin: overproduction, struggle, variation, natural selection, new species.
Germinal variations are inherited, somatic ones are not.
